title: The 8 Levels of Walking Home in the Dark
house: A bustling neon-lit metropolis where fruit and vegetable people commute on crowded subway lines and walk past rainy asphalt streets.

levels.name: Mia, 21, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 1. Level 1: 120 euros left in my bank account and three blocks of dark alleyway ahead. My skin is a pale green pear, trembling in the cold midnight fog. I tap my cracked smartphone, pressing it hard against my ear as I walk past the abandoned subway station. Hello, yes Dad, I am right at the corner of 5th Avenue, just two minutes away. My footsteps echo loudly on the wet concrete. Suddenly, a cold draft sweeps through the corridor, carrying the sharp scent of ozone and copper. I quicken my pace, but the shadows seem to stretch unnaturally along the brick walls. Is someone following my tracks, or is it just the wind playing tricks on my exhausted mind? Hey little pear, who are you pretending to talk to when your screen is completely black? You are walking alone because nobody cares about a zero. My heart drops into my stomach as the phone suddenly vibrates with an incoming text from an unknown sender. The glowing screen reveals a live camera feed of my exact location, and the heavy security gate at the end of the alley begins to slide shut. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 2. Level 2: 850 euros monthly rent and a two-mile night walk past the industrial district. My orange peel skin is damp from the cold drizzle, and my cheap plastic earbuds hang uselessly around my neck. I pretend to chat animatedly with my mom about lasagna recipes, talking loudly into empty air. The streetlamps flicker overhead, buzzing like angry hornets in the damp night air. I clutch my thermal coffee flask tighter, wishing I had enough cash for a late-night taxi ride. Why are you shouting at your pocket in the dark, orange boy? Save your breath, nobody listens to beggars in the rain. A sleek black sedan rolls slowly beside the curb, its tinted windows winding down with a mechanical hum. A gloved hand tosses a heavy leather envelope at my feet before speeding off into the foggy tunnel. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 3. Level 3: 2,400 euros freelance salary and a terrifying four-block stretch past the dark park. My strawberry skin is dotted with tiny seeds, glistening under the neon sign of an all-night diner. I hold my phone up high, talking loudly into the speaker about quarterly tax returns and client meetings. The autumn wind howls through the metal branches of the oak trees, making the shadows dance like frantic specters. Every footstep behind me matches my own cadence, creating a chilling echo in the deserted street. Look at this amateur trying to sound corporate in an empty street. Confidence cannot be faked when your badge is that small. A sharp siren wails in the distance, and the neon sign above the diner abruptly explodes in a shower of blue sparks, plunging the sidewalk into absolute darkness. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Marcus, 29, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 4. Level 4: 4,500 euros net salary and a midnight shortcut through the old railway tunnels. My glossy Red Apple skin gleams under the emergency tunnel lights, and my designer wool coat keeps out the biting chill. I hold my phone to my ear, pretending to discuss stock portfolios with my fictitious investment broker. The damp concrete walls drip with oily water, and the metallic tang of rust fills the stagnant air around me. I check my watch, realizing the tunnel shouldn't be open at this hour. Who are you trying to impress in an abandoned tunnel, little fruit? Money cannot buy you an exit when the tunnel doors lock from the outside. A massive steel bulkhead slams shut behind me with a thunderous crash, trapping me in the pitch-black corridor with only my glowing forehead badge for light. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 5. Level 5: 3,100 euros project fee and a late-night walk past the construction zone. My smooth Avocado skin is cool, but sweat beads near my collar as scaffolding creaks in the wind. I press my phone against my ear, pretending to chew out a contractor. Towering cranes loom overhead like prehistoric skeletons against the bruised purple sky. A stray cat darts across the gravel, scattering rusted tools that clatter against the chain-link fence. What are you shouting about on the sidewalk, avocado boy? Mid-tier numbers always make the loudest noise in the dark. A floodlight suddenly snaps on, blinding me with a harsh white glare, and a security drone hums aggressively as it descends right in front of my face. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 6. Level 6: 6,800 euros monthly corporate paycheck and a lonely walk past the financial district towers. My Broccoli head is tightly packed, standing tall inside my rigid dark suit. I hold my phone to my ear, talking loudly about corporate mergers to an empty dial tone. The towering glass skyscrapers reflect distorted funhouse versions of my silhouette against the polished granite pavement. A cold gust of wind rattles the revolving glass doors of an empty bank lobby. Who are you trying to impress with that fake corporate jargon, designer girl? A high salary cannot buy you respect when everyone knows you are a fraud. The digital clock on the towering stock exchange ticker suddenly freezes at midnight, and all the automatic doors unlock simultaneously with a synchronized click. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 7. Level 7: 9.200 euros monthly executive bonus and a private stroll past the luxury penthouse balconies. My bright Lemon skin is smooth and bright, glowing fiercely against the dark velvet night. I hold my phone to my ear, effortlessly managing my corporate empire in fluent French. The panoramic city lights stretch out below like a sea of burning embers, beautiful yet completely sterile. I hear the faint hum of a helicopter hovering somewhere above the cloud layer. Watch where you are walking, coffee boy, before you scratch my bumper. Your high number means nothing when your engine is running on empty. A private elevator bell chimes loudly in the middle of the empty plaza, its doors parting to reveal an ascending path straight into the upper atmosphere. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Magnus, 42, Mogul
levels.story: The 8 levels of walking home in the dark. Level 8. Level 8: 25,000 euros daily passive income and the entire city bowing down at my feet. My Crown Jewel Pineapple head gleams with golden facets, radiating absolute power across the midnight skyline. I don't need to pretend to make phone calls anymore; my phone rings constantly with people begging for my attention. Every single person I passed in the dark were all just stepping stones on my path to the top. The wind up here whispers secrets of ancient fortunes and fallen empires, reminding me that absolute power is a lonely throne. Below me, millions of glowing numbers pulse in the dark like constellations of trapped souls. The number on your forehead never lies, but it is never the whole truth. Suddenly, all the numbers across the entire metropolis flicker simultaneously, turning blood red before every single digital badge in the city shorts out completely, plunging the world into total, unreadable darkness. Which topic should we explore in the next 8-level series?
